title: RelayLLM: Efficient Reasoning via Collaborative Decoding

The large model then generates the next n n tokens (or stops early if an end-of-sequence “[EOS]” token is reached), providing a high-quality continuation or reasoning step. After ℳ L \mathcal{M}_{L} completes the generation, control is returned to the small model. The context is updated with the new tokens generated by ℳ L \mathcal{M}_{L} added into the existing context. Unlike the large model, ℳ S \mathcal{M}_{S} retains the full history, including its own generated command tokens (<call>n</call>). This allows ℳ S \mathcal{M}_{S} to maintain a trace of its active delegation decisions. With the updated context, ℳ S \mathcal{M}_{S} resumes generation, digesting the expert’s guidance to continue the reasoning process. To enable the small model ℳ S \mathcal{M}_{S} to determine when and how long to invoke the LLM, we propose a two-stage framework including a supervised warm-up phase followed by a reinforcement learning phase. The small model ℳ S \mathcal{M}_{S} may not naturally generate the command pattern 𝒞 cmd \mathcal{C}_{\text{cmd}} if we train it directly with reinforcement learning. We employ a supervised warm-up phase as cold start to initialize the model with the necessary structural knowledge. We construct a synthetic dataset 𝒟 warm \mathcal{D}_{\text{warm}} to teach the model the calling command without inducing distribution shifts.
